name: Sensors (engine & driveline monitoring)
description: The electrical system's sensor map. OE engine-control sensors (crank, cam, knock, MAP/TMAP, IAT, ECT, fuel-rail pressure, throttle position, oil pressure) are physically owned by the engine system and are referenced here; this subsystem adds the race monitoring sensors: oil pressure/temperature (logged and alarmed), low-side fuel pressure, coolant pressure, crankcase pressure, EGT per cylinder, transmission and differential temperatures, charge-air temperature and fuel level.

components.name: OE engine sensor interface (reference list)
components.description: Wiring interface to the GM Gen V LT engine-control sensors. Each sensor is mounted on the engine (see engine system ids) and wired through the engine harness. Typical LT1/LT4 set: crankshaft position (rear of block, 58X), camshaft position (front cover, 4X), 2 knock sensors (valley/ block sides), MAP/TMAP (intake/supercharger inlet & outlet on LT4), MAF/IAT (intake tube – kit-supplied), ECT (head), electronic throttle body position (2 tracks), fuel-rail pressure (DI high side – 3-pin late / 4-pin early sensor), low-side fuel pressure (kit-supplied), oil pressure (kit or engine), VVT cam phaser solenoid feedback via cam sensor.
components.location: On the engine – see engine ids.

factory.name: GM Gen V LT sensor set
factory.notes: Holley notes early vs late LT4 by the fuel-rail pressure sensor connector (4-pin early, 3-pin late) – the ECU/harness kit must match.

hardware.item: OE sensor connectors (crank, cam, knock, MAP, ECT, FRP, ETC)
hardware.spec: OE sealed connectors with CPA locks – fastener torques owned by engine system

installNotes: Verify each sensor's connector type against the chosen ECU harness (early/late LT4 differences).
inspection: Check sensor plausibility in ECU data at key-on and idle.

sources.title: Holley Gen V LT DI early/late identification

components.name: Oil pressure sensor (race, logged & alarmed)
components.description: Dedicated 0–10 bar (0–150 psi) sealed pressure transducer on the main oil gallery or dry-sump pressure manifold, wired to the dash/logger with an rpm-dependent low-pressure alarm (and optionally an engine-protection strategy in the ECU). The OE sensor can remain for the ECU.
components.location: Oil filter housing / dry-sump remote filter outlet or block gallery port (engine-bay, x≈0.0–0.3, y≈0.35, z≈±0.25).

factory.name: GM oil pressure sensor (in kit or engine)

raceOptions.name: Bosch Motorsport PSS-10 / Texense / MoTeC sealed pressure sensor
raceOptions.notes: Use a remote-mount on a braided -3 hose to isolate from engine vibration.

hardware.torque: 1/8 NPT: 2–3 turns past finger tight; M10x1 w/ washer ~15 N·m
hardware.threadlocker: thread sealant (PTFE paste) on NPT only

installNotes: Remote-mount the sensor on a bracket with a short -3 braided hose to avoid vibration failures.
inspection: Leaks; reading at hot idle vs baseline.

modelRef.dimensions: M10 x 1 thread, ~Ø20 x 60 mm incl. connector.
modelRef.features: Stainless hex and body, plastic connector.

components.name: Oil temperature sensor
components.description: NTC temperature sensor in the oil feed (after cooler) or dry-sump tank outlet; logged and alarmed (e.g. > 130 °C).
components.location: Oil cooler outlet line / dry-sump tank.

factory.name: GM engine oil temperature sensor (where fitted)

raceOptions.name: Bosch NTC M12x1.5 / 1/8 NPT temperature sensor

hardware.spec: M12 x 1.5 with copper washer or 1/8 NPT

modelRef.dimensions: M12 x 1.5 / 1/8 NPT NTC, ~19 mm hex, ~45 mm long.
modelRef.features: Brass thread and hex, plastic connector body.

components.name: Low-side fuel pressure sensor
components.description: Measures feed pressure to the cam-driven high-pressure DI pump (the Chevrolet Performance kit includes the low-side sensor the E92 uses for pump-module PWM control). Add a logged sensor for data if the kit sensor is ECU-only.
components.location: Feed line near the HP pump on the engine (valley/rear of engine).

factory.name: GM fuel pressure sensor (in LT controller kit)

hardware.spec: Per sensor (OE quick-connect tee or 1/8 NPT)

sources.title: LT4 kit contents incl. fuel pressure sensor

components.name: Coolant pressure sensor
components.description: Detects head-gasket failure (pressure spikes) and cap/hose leaks (pressure loss) – often the first warning on a race engine.
components.location: Coolant crossover / thermostat housing or a tee in the upper hose.

hardware.spec: Aluminum hose tee with 1/8 NPT port + hose clamps

components.name: Crankcase pressure sensor
components.description: Measures crankcase vacuum (dry-sump scavenge effectiveness) or blow-by; useful to diagnose ring seal and scavenge problems.
components.location: Valve cover or dry-sump breather port.
installNotes: Remote-mount above the port so oil drains back.

components.name: Exhaust gas temperature probes (per cylinder)
components.description: K-type thermocouples in each primary ~50–75 mm from the port, via a CAN thermocouple amplifier (e.g. 8-channel). Shows cylinder-to-cylinder fuel/ignition imbalance – especially useful on DI where per-cylinder trims are possible.
components.location: Each header primary near the flange, both banks.

raceOptions.name: MoTeC E816/ TCA thermocouple amplifier / ECUMaster EGT-to-CAN

installNotes: Equal insertion depth on all probes (~1/3 tube diameter).
inspection: Probe tip erosion; lead heat damage.

modelRef.dimensions: K-type probe Ø3–6 mm with 1/8 NPT compression fitting (7/16" hex).
modelRef.features: Stainless probe, brass compression fitting, stainless transition, braided lead.

components.name: Transmission & differential temperature sensors
components.description: NTC temperature sensors in the transmission and diff (sump or cooler outlet) to manage cooler pumps/fans and alarm.
components.location: Transmission case (x≈0.9, y≈0.30) and rear diff cover (x≈2.85, y≈0.33).

modelRef.features: Brass thread and hex, plastic connector.

components.name: Charge-air temperature sensor (post intercooler, LT4)
components.description: Supercharged LT4 has intercooler bricks in the supercharger housing; charge-air temperature after the cooler is critical for knock margin and intercooler-pump/heat-exchanger performance. Usually an OE TMAP on the supercharger outlet; add a logged sensor if the ECU doesn't share it.

modelRef.features: Plastic body with sensing nipple, connector shroud, mounting tab.

components.name: Fuel level sender
components.description: Resistive or capacitive level sender in the fuel cell (or OE tank sender in the pump module) read by the dash for fuel-remaining and low-fuel alarm; combine with ECU fuel-used calculation for endurance strategy.
components.location: Fuel cell top plate (trunk) or OE tank module.

factory.name: GM fuel pump module level sensor (MU2369 module for ZL1, per Aeromotive)

hardware.spec: #10-24 or M5 screws with sealing washers

installNotes: Calibrate with known fuel volumes (5 L steps).

sources.title: Aeromotive ZL1 PWM controller (Gen 6 module MU2369)

modelRef.dimensions: Capacitive probe ~300 mm long through the cell top plate, Ø~50 mm flange (estimated).
modelRef.features: Aluminium probe tube, 5-bolt flange, connector on top.
